title: DestructiveFindings
description: Sidecar artifact for destructive / fuzz / chaos campaigns. Lives next to the standard benchmark-result.json. Captures crash/OOM/hang counts, post-attack liveness probe, RSS/native-heap deltas, and a degradation classification. Destructive findings are EXPLORATORY by construction: results are never comparison_eligible and must not enter the comparative aggregation pipeline.

run_id.description: Matches the run_id of the paired BenchmarkResult artifact.

scenario.description: Scenario id from docs/scenario-catalog.md (e.g. fuzz-http1-parser, destructive-slowloris-h1).

duration_seconds.description: Wall-clock duration of the attack/fuzz window (excluding warmup/cooldown).

claim_scope.description: Destructive findings are never comparison_eligible. Locked to exploratory.

comparison_axis.description: Destructive runs do not enter cross-tier or within-tier comparison axes.

iterations_total.description: Total fuzz iterations / attack requests dispatched.

crash_count.description: Unexpected throwables from the SUT (excluding whitelisted parse exceptions). Each is a finding.

oom_count.description: Iterations where the SUT threw OutOfMemoryError or the JVM exited with OOM-killed.

hang_count.description: Iterations that exceeded the per-iteration timeout WHILE THE TARGET OWED AN ANSWER -- i.e. the payload completed a request. A timeout on a payload that never terminated its request is incomplete_wait_count, not this. Before that split (2026-08-26) this field counted both, and a campaign whose mutants are ~10 % truncated logged a double-digit hang_count against a target answering its liveness probe in 8 ms.

incomplete_wait_count.description: Iterations that timed out on a payload which did NOT complete a request: the target is correctly waiting for the rest of it and the ATTACKER gave up at its socket deadline. NOT a finding, and deliberately structured rather than left in `notes` -- burying it in prose is how it was mistaken for hang_count in the first place. It does not establish that the target is healthy: whether a target ever times out an incomplete request is what destructive-slowloris-h1 measures.

connections_opened.description: destructive-slowloris-h1 only: half-open connections the attacker established.

connections_dropped.description: destructive-slowloris-h1 only: how many of those the TARGET closed during the attack window -- the one measurement this scenario exists to make. It is also what licenses the `incomplete-wait` outcome in the radamsa drivers: a target that never evicts a half-open connection inside 120 s cannot have been the source of a 2 s attacker-side timeout. The runner read this value from the attacker and then discarded it until 2026-08-27, so the first slowloris artifact recorded connections_dropped nowhere and left `notes` null.

outcome_details.description: Per-outcome detail histogram, protocol-specific. For destructive-radamsa-h2 the keys are the target's GOAWAY/RST_STREAM error codes (e.g. "GOAWAY:FRAME_SIZE_ERROR", "GOAWAY:COMPRESSION_ERROR"), which name the layer that rejected the mutant -- framing vs HPACK -- and are the only positive evidence an all-zero crash/hang campaign produces. Absent for H1, whose classifier has no equivalent signal.

unique_crash_signatures.description: Distinct stack-trace top-frames among recorded crashes.

mean_time_to_crash_us.description: Mean microseconds from attack start to first observed crash; null if no crashes.

leak_count_delta.description: (MemoryStats.leakCount after) - (MemoryStats.leakCount before). Negative if pool released more than expected.

liveness_probe.description: Post-attack clean-traffic liveness probe. Mandatory for slowloris/radamsa/arena-lifecycle campaigns.

protocol.description: Protocol the post-attack liveness probe actually spoke. Until 2026-08-26 every probe was plain curl, i.e. HTTP/1.1, including destructive-radamsa-h2 -- so an attack that broke the HTTP/2 frame parser while HTTP/1.1 kept answering would have been recorded as survival. An h2/h2c probe answered over HTTP/1.1 now fails instead of passing quietly.

asserted_alive.description: true iff status_code == expected_status AND duration_ms <= expected_max_response_ms.

resource_delta.description: Process resource snapshot before vs after attack window. Optional for jazzer-parser (in-process JMH-like) campaigns.

jfr_recording_path.description: Path to the JFR recording covering the attack window. NEVER published in public mode.

baseline_warmup_seconds.description: Seconds of clean traffic driven BEFORE rss_bytes_before was sampled. 0 or null means the baseline was taken on a target that had never served a request, so first-load JIT, metaspace fill and heap commit are charged to the attack -- measured at +34.9 % RSS on a run whose post-GC live heap was 9.5 MB. Two runs with different values here are not comparable on rss_bytes_delta.

rss_series_samples.description: Number of RSS samples taken across the attack window. null or 0 means no series was recorded, and any claim about growth CORRELATING WITH DURATION is then unsupported by this artifact.

rss_series_early_slope_bytes_per_s.description: Least-squares RSS slope over the first half of the attack window.

rss_series_late_slope_bytes_per_s.description: Least-squares RSS slope over the second half. This pair is the leak-vs-plateau discriminator the arena-lifecycle-leak scenario's FAIL condition requires: a leak holds the late slope near the early one, first-load growth collapses it toward zero. A single before/after delta cannot distinguish them.

degradation_class.description: Observed failure/degradation classification. 'stable' = target absorbed attack and liveness probe passed within tolerance.

tool_versions.description: Pinned versions of attack tooling (jazzer, radamsa, slowloris-driver) and kernel artifact under test.

seeds.description: Reproducibility seeds. Without these the campaign is not reproducible and the artifact is descriptive-only.

tolerance.description: Scenario-declared tolerance thresholds that produced the degradation_class.

publication_mode.description: Destructive findings sidecars are locked to internal-only publication. Crash inputs and raw attack corpora may contain attacker-supplied bytes and are blocked in public/redacted modes by publish-report.sh.
